author: Zach Rosson
title: Deliberately forgotten: internet shutdowns with no end
content:
Content note: The following post contains references to war crimes, sexual assault, murder, and death

.







There is a complete lack of transparency.










Cutting the internet means cutting us off from the outside world.










I can say that the internet and communications blackout were as impactful as the bombings, destruction, and killings.










These are the words of people who have experienced years-long 

internet shutdowns with no end in sight

. Alarmingly, the number of such prolonged shutdowns has steadily risen each year, as perpetrators around the world quietly decide to 

keep people cut off from the internet indefinitely

.
















For more information about ongoing shutdowns, explore our new dashboard 

below

.




As we write, people in parts of Myanmar continue facing repeated and prolonged internet shutdowns 

amid deadly violence

, as the junta’s 

control and surveillance of communications networks

 creates an “

internet dead zone

” where few dare to speak openly against the regime. In Tigray, Ethiopia, meanwhile, 

new internet shutdowns

 are raising fears that the same population that was 

cut off from the internet for over two years during a bloody civil war

 will once again be disconnected and in even greater danger. And 

the list goes on

.

author: Amina Khan
title: Beware of spyware: Access Now urges pension funds to scrutinize investments for spyware exposure
content:
On September 28, 2026, Access Now wrote to four pension funds — 

Los Angeles County Employees Retirement Association

, 

Houston Firefighters’ Relief and Retirement Fund

, 

New Mexico Educational Retirement Board

, and  

Hampshire Pension Fund

 — regarding their investment in AE Industrial Partners (AEI). AEI 

purchased

 spyware technology vendor Paragon Solutions in 2024 and merged the company with its holding company REDLattice. The letters urge pension fund managers to use their leverage with AEI to ensure the fund “provide[s] remedy where warranted, and implement robust safeguards” to prevent any contribution to human rights breaches.













Investors have a responsibility to identify and address human rights risks in their portfolios. Paragon presents a clear risk given its appalling human rights record, and these pension funds should avoid exposure to such spyware in their portfolios and demand answers from AE Industrial Partners.




Isedua Oribhabor, Business & Human Rights Manager at Access Now

well-documented history

The Collaboration on International ICT Policy in East and Southern Africa (CIPESA), 

will host

 the Forum on Internet Freedom in Africa 2026 (FIFAfrica26) set to take place on 

September 28- October 1, 2026

 in Mauritius.




Over the past decade, the FIFAfrica conference 

has provided

 a space for connection and conversation and garnered a track record of bringing together multi-stakeholder actors and shared efforts aimed at advancing rights, freedoms, participation, and innovation in the digital sphere. As open spaces for human rights conversations continue to shrink, convenings such as these are more important than ever.




Access Now has been a key partner of CIPESA and continues to actively participate in FIFAfrica to strengthen our partnership and expand our network within Africa and beyond. We are happy to be part of this year’s FIFAfrica.
